land.text: Ranthambore: 'Govinda then established a new kingdom with its capital at Ranastambhapura (modern Ranthambor)'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Chahamanas of Shakambhari'. The Chauhan dossier calls the grant a fief; the Ranastambhapura page says Govindaraja 'agreed to rule as a vassal of the Ghurids in 1192' at Ajmer, was dethroned there by Hari-raja, and then founded the Ranthambore kingdom.

land.text: Ranthambore, whose fort Alauddin Khalji captured in July 1301 and gave to Ulugh Khan as governor

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Delhi Sultanate'. The Khalji dossier's 1301 gain uses an 80 km disc round the fort; the page is silent on a formal annexation.

capitals.name: Ranastambhapura (Ranthambore)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Ranastambhapura'; 'a new kingdom with its capital at Ranastambhapura (modern Ranthambor)'. No capital move is recorded; coordinates are the gazetteer's Ranthambore.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for the Ranthambore branch (its Chauhan Dynasty row runs 980-1201 round Ajmer). The infobox gives no area and the page says only that the dynasty ruled 'the area around their capital'; the 60 km disc (about 11,000 km2) is the radius the Chauhan dossier hands over. The Hammiradeva page (opened for the extent) gives no territory beyond 'a kingdom centred around Ranthambore'; Hammira's raids on Bhimarasa, Mandalgarh, Dhar, Abu and Pushkar are undated tribute and plunder, not annexations, and are not drawn.

correction.text: Ranthambore, until the fort fell on 10 July 1301

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the last year: the same disc, the state's last cells before the Khalji conquest (the Khalji dossier's gain is the 80 km disc).

ledger.note: 1192: Govindaraja founds the Ranthambore branch of the Chahamanas. Infobox 'Established: 1192'; he 'agreed to rule as a vassal of the Ghurids in 1192', was dethroned at Ajmer by Hari-raja, and 'then established a new kingdom with its capital at Ranastambhapura (modern Ranthambor)'. The page dates the establishment, not the move to Ranthambore.

1226: Iltutmish takes Ranthambore. 'Iltumish captured the fort in 1226 CE.' The page notes Balhana, Govindaraja's son, 'is recorded as a vassal of the Delhi Sultan Iltumish in 1215 CE' and later declared independence. Only the fort is drawn lost; the page does not say the countryside went.

region.text: the fort of Ranthambore, recaptured by Vagbhata

ledger.note: 1236 (bridging year): Vagbhata retakes Ranthambore. 'He recaptured Ranthambore during the reign of the Delhi ruler Razia (r. 1236-1240).' The page gives the span 1236-1240, not the year; the first year is used. The Mamluk dossier records no matching loss.

region.text: Ranthambore and its fort, taken by Alauddin Khalji

ledger.note: July 1301: Ranthambore falls to Alauddin Khalji. 'Facing a desperate situation, in July 1301, Hammira and his loyal companions came out of the fort, and fought to death'; Firishta dates the capture to 10 July 1301, and Alauddin 'appointed Ulugh Khan as its governor'.

region.text: Ranthambore, passing to the Delhi Sultanate under Alauddin Khalji

ledger.note: 1301: the Ranastambhapura Chahamanas end. 'The dynasty ended with his defeat against the Delhi Sultan Alauddin Khalji at the Siege of Ranthambore in 1301'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1301'. The page lists Hammira as '(1283-1311)' but dates the end to 1301; the Hammiradeva page gives his death as 10 July 1301.

wars.name: Iltutmish's capture of Ranthambore
wars.outcome: Iltutmish captures the fort in 1226; Vagbhata recaptures it in Razia's reign (1236-1240).
wars.note: No article of its own; the page gives only the capture year.

wars.name: Jalaluddin Khalji's invasions of Ranthambore
wars.outcome: Jalaluddin Khalji invades Hammira's territory in 1290 and Jhain in 1292, unsuccessfully; no land changes hands.
wars.note: The Hammiradeva page: 'In 1290, Jalaluddin Khalji ... invaded Hammira's territory' and 'In 1292 ... once again invaded Jhain, this time unsuccessfully'.

wars.name: Siege of Ranthambore (1301)
wars.outcome: Alauddin Khalji captures the fort in July 1301 after Nusrat Khan is killed and Hammira dies fighting; Ulugh Khan is appointed governor.
wars.note: The siege page dates neither the start of the siege nor Nusrat Khan's death; only July 1301 for the end.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the kingdom is a radius round Ranthambore.

sources.title: Hammiradeva
sources.note: Accession 1283/1285, raids to 1288, Jalaluddin 1290 and 1292, extent only 'centred around Ranthambore'.

notes: No Cliopatria row; the branch is drawn as a 60 km disc round Ranthambore (the radius the Chauhan dossier hands over), with the fort (50 km, the Mamluk dossier's disc) lost 1226 and regained under Razia (1236-1240; first year used, confidence 1). The Mamluk dossier has the 1226 gain but no loss of Ranthambore c.1236-1240, and the Khalji dossier's 1301 gain is an 80 km coordinate disc: a gap-filler should add the Mamluk loss. Hammira's conquests (Bhimarasa, Mandalgarh, Ujjain, Dhar, Abu, Vardhanapura, Pushkar) are undated on the Hammiradeva page and are tribute raids ('until 1288'), so no gain is drawn; the Ranastambhapura page says only that he 'conquered Pushkara and Shakambari', undated. The Chahamanas page lists Hammira as '(1283-1311)' but ends the dynasty in 1301. No ruler list with reign years exists on the pages opened (only Govindaraja 1192 and Hammira), so no rulers strip. The Chauhan dossier calls Govindaraja's Ranthambore a Ghurid 'fief'; this page says vassal at Ajmer then a new kingdom. The 1192-1226 vassalage to the Ghurids and Balhana's 1215 vassalage to Iltutmish belong to the suzerains' dossiers (vassal_start in the Ghurid dossier would carry the first); not recorded here because no ledger type records being a vassal.
